extracted.intended_audience: community newspaper editors, local journalists, and journalism researchers
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and implicit standards for selecting and evaluating local/community newspaper stories that promote social cohesion and community identity. Focuses on what beats/topics local papers cover and why those stories matter for trust, belonging, and civic participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Civic-Building Stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Coverage of local government and civic processes that enable citizens to participate in community governance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include local government meetings, school board decisions, local elections, tax/budget issues, and public health updates. These stories are oriented toward civic-action enabling — providing information citizens need to participate in local civic life and fostering participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community-Identity Stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories that affirm community identity by highlighting local people, events, and milestones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include local festivals and parades, high school sports, hometown person profiles, anniversaries and retirements, births, weddings, and obituaries. Such coverage is identity-affirming and trust-building by naming neighbors and profiling locals, which enhances belonging and the community's 'we' feeling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local Economic Stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting on the local economic conditions and events that affect residents' livelihoods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include new businesses, layoffs at major employers, real estate developments, and local agriculture/industry. These stories inform residents about economic opportunities and threats, contributing to practical knowledge for local decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical Service
rubrics_metrics.description: Timely, utility-oriented information that helps residents navigate everyday disruptions and safety issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include weather affecting locals, road closures, power outages, school closings, and neighborhood crime. Emphasizes practical utility — information you can act on — and directly supports residents' daily needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyperlocal Pride
rubrics_metrics.description: Coverage that cultivates local pride by spotlighting local achievements and heroes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include achievements by locals receiving national recognition, hometown sports team coverage, and stories about local heroes. This community-celebrating coverage strengthens collective identity and fosters positive feelings about the community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic specificity (Hyperlocal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Criterion that stories be geographically specific and targeted to the immediate community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes hyperlocal focus — stories that matter to people in the same town or neighborhood rather than regional/national audiences. Geographic specificity distinguishes community newsworthiness from national news criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Civic-action enabling
rubrics_metrics.description: Criterion that reporting supplies the information citizens need to participate in civic life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories should enable action (e.g., knowledge of meetings, election information, public health guidance). This is tied to promoting participation in local civic life and strengthening democratic engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identity-affirming
rubrics_metrics.description: Criterion that coverage affirms a shared community identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes profiling locals, celebrating community traditions, and telling stories that communicate 'us' — which enhances belonging and reduces social isolation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trust-building
rubrics_metrics.description: Criterion that journalism should build interpersonal trust within the community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trust-building practices include naming neighbors, profiling local actors, and consistently reporting on local issues in ways that increase interpersonal trust and credibility among residents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical utility
rubrics_metrics.description: Criterion that news provide usable information residents can act upon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on service journalism (alerts, closures, safety information) that has immediate, actionable value to community members, thereby reducing risk and facilitating daily life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community-celebrating
rubrics_metrics.description: Criterion that journalism highlight and celebrate positive aspects of the local community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Positive coverage of local achievements, events, and people contributes to pride and strengthens the community's collective identity and 'we' feeling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social cohesion outcomes as evaluation goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Community newspaper success should be measured by its contribution to social cohesion outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Yamamoto identifies specific desired outcomes: increases in interpersonal trust within the community, enhanced belonging, promotion of participation in local civic life, reduction of social isolation, and strengthening of the community 'we' feeling. These outcomes provide evaluative guidance for prioritizing story selection and newsroom goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Different evaluation standard from national outlets
rubrics_metrics.description: Principle that community newspapers require evaluation criteria distinct from those used for national news organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implication: newsworthiness for local papers must include cohesion-promoting and identity-affirming stories that national editors might dismiss as trivial. Evaluation should weigh local social-psychological benefits alongside traditional journalistic metrics.
